title: After knee replacement when you are frail: rehabilitation at home (UK)
meta_title: After knee replacement when you are frail: rehabilitation at home
meta_description: Recovering from knee replacement when frail: exercises, pain relief, swelling, safety at home, and warning signs to report after surgery.
excerpt: Recovering from knee replacement when frail: exercises, pain relief, swelling, safety at home, and warning signs to report after surgery.
direct_answer: Recovery after knee replacement takes time, especially with frailty. Regular exercises from your physiotherapist, managing pain and swelling, safe movement at home and help with daily tasks all support recovery. Report signs of infection or a blood clot promptly.
author: Louis Maxwell
reviewer_credentials: First Contact Practitioner, HCPC PH128483, CSP member

content:
Frailty can make recovery slower, but steady practice helps.

This guide covers recovery at home. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Exercises

Do the exercises your physiotherapist gives you, little and often.

Pain relief and swelling

  • Take pain relief as advised so you can exercise.
  • Raise your leg and use ice if advised.

Tablets, topical options and what not to DIY

Ask your pharmacist before adding over-the-counter painkillers. Do not change prescribed blood thinners or pain medicines yourself.

Safety at home

  • Clear routes.
  • Use your walking aid.
  • Have help for the first weeks.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain or sudden breathlessness.
  • Contact your surgical team or NHS 111 urgently if the wound is red, hot or leaking, you have a fever, or your calf is swollen and painful.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

How long does recovery take?

Often several months.

Is pain normal?

Some pain is expected; report severe or worsening pain.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Physiotherapy
